name: Pin an Agent Version and Override Model, Context and Idempotency Per Call
query: Our deployed `planner` agent has versions 1 and 2. From the `release_notes` workflow I need to: pin v2 for now, use `gpt-4o` for this call only, hand the agent the release metadata as structured data rather than pasting it into the prompt, make workflow retries not spawn a second agent run, and group all calls for one customer so I can find them later. Show me the AGENT task.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/workflow-definition.md `### AGENT` (per-call override row: `version`, `sessionId`, `context{}`, `media[]`, `model`, `timeoutSeconds`, `idempotencyKey`, `credentials{}`) and references/agents.md §8 operate / §12 gotchas (`sessionId` groups but does not replay history).
Step 2: Confirm the versions exist: `conductor agent get planner --version 2` (or `GET /api/agent/planner?version=2`).

Step 3: `AGENT` task with `agentType: "conductor"`, `name: "planner"`, `version: 2` (omitting `version` means latest — pinning protects the workflow from a later deploy), `prompt` from workflow input.

Step 4: `model: "openai/gpt-4o"` as a per-call override — `provider/model` form (Rule 11 / F6); the provider must be `configured: true` in `GET /api/providers/status`; this does not change the deployed definition.

Step 5: `context: {"release": "${workflow.input.release}"}` passes structured data the agent sees as context (the compiled agent exposes it as `${...output.output.context}`), keeping the prompt short.

Step 6: `idempotencyKey`: the task already defaults to `conductor-agent-<workflowId>:<taskRef>:<iteration>`, so a retry of the same task reuses the run; set an explicit key (e.g. `"release-${workflow.input.releaseId}"`) when re-runs of the whole workflow must also map to one agent run.

Step 7: `sessionId: "${workflow.input.customerId}"` — it becomes the output `contextId` and groups executions (`conductor agent execution`, `GET /api/agent/executions?sessionId=`), but it does not replay earlier turns into a new run: whatever the next call needs must be in `prompt` or `context`.

Step 8: Bounds and outputs: `maxDurationSeconds` (F1) and optional `timeoutSeconds` for the agent's own wall clock; read `${<ref>.output.text}` / `${<ref>.output.output.result}`; write the JSON to a file, `conductor workflow create <file>`.
success_criteria: Pins `version: 2` and explains that omitting `version` resolves to the latest deployed version
Uses a per-call `model` override in `provider/model` form (e.g. `openai/gpt-4o`) and notes the provider must be configured on the server
Passes the release metadata via `context: {...}` (structured) rather than only concatenating it into the prompt
Uses `idempotencyKey` (explicit, or explains the automatic per-task default) so retries do not start a second agent run
Uses `sessionId` for grouping and states that it groups executions (`contextId`) but does not replay prior conversation history into a new run
Verifies the version exists with `conductor agent get planner --version 2` or the equivalent REST call
Sets `maxDurationSeconds` (and/or a workflow timeout), citing F1 or the 24 h default
Reads the result via `${<ref>.output.text}` or `${<ref>.output.output.result}` and writes the JSON to a file before registering
Does not put a framework name in `agentType` and does not claim `CONDUCTOR_AGENT_LLM_MODEL` controls the per-call model
